title: Accenture caps staff Claude spending at $29 a month, 404 Media reports
source_used: The Next Web (relaying 404 Media's report of 15 Oct 2026)
key_facts: 404 Media's Joseph Cox reported on 15 Oct 2026 that Accenture now pays only $29 a month per person for Claude use.
The change took effect on 1 Oct, according to an internal announcement 404 Media has seen, titled 'Claude Enterprise Users: Important Updates to Licensing and Usage Costs'.
Some employees had been spending as much as $1,000 a month; above $29 they must charge the extra use to a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), Accenture's budget code for a project or team.
Premium plans come with $250 of token usage a week; many employees are on the General plan.
Some employees want Premium accounts so their projects avoid the extra charge; one said usage costs were above $500, another $500 to $1,000 a month, and a third said access was revoked.
An Accenture spokesperson told 404 Media the company makes AI available to all its people and continues to invest in AI capabilities.
Accenture has about 799,000 people and about 9,000 clients, by its own figures; the announcement cited its survey in which 82% of more than 3,000 executives are raising AI investment.
Microsoft set AI budgets for its divisions in August and Atlassian's engineers work to an AI budget.
quote_evidence: The consulting firm now pays only $29 a month per person for Claude use, Joseph Cox reported for 404 Media on 15 October.
Some Accenture employees had been spending as much as $1,000 a month.
Other companies have already moved to cap employee AI spending.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows a big AI adopter rationing staff use of a paid AI tool, a cost signal for other enterprises.
event_date: Cap in force from 1 Oct 2026; first reported by 404 Media on 15 Oct 2026
notes: Original reporter is 404 Media; The Next Web (pool item) relays it. Accenture's cap rests on an internal announcement seen by 404 Media, not a public statement.
